levers.min_reform_lever: Single interagency board-effectiveness assessment.

operands: OCC App. D III.F board self-assessment

levers.rationale: The lever collapses parallel Fed (SR 21-3 / LFI) and OCC (App. D III.F) board self-assessment processes into one interagency board-effectiveness assessment. This is the classic consolidation shape: MERGE the parallel duties, CANONICALIZE_DEFINITION so one standard governs, and RESOLVE_CROSS_REFERENCE to align the sources. The roadmap names FRB + OCC acting via a joint statement (interagency_statement), with FDI Act \u00a739 as the touched statute proposed for the floor. Legal distinctness is minimal, supporting merger rather than parallel_distinct_purpose retention.

levers.min_reform_lever: Cross-reference manual to the rule; avoid restating. v2.1: resolve the two unreconciled pending rewrites (2024 proposals add a freestanding board-oversight standard + annual ratification; 2026 proposals permit approval by the board, an equivalent body, or senior management) before they compound the layering.
levers.rationale: Source supports a bare cross-reference action ('Cross-reference manual to the rule; avoid restating'), which alone maps to RESOLVE_CROSS_REFERENCE. However the operative v2.1 instruction adds resolution of 'two unreconciled pending rewrites' with conflicting content (2024: 'a freestanding board-oversight standard + annual ratification'; 2026: 'approval by the board, an equivalent body, or senior management'). Because the text presents these as unreconciled and does not settle which prevails, the lever cannot be reduced to one primitive or one named composite; it is a genuine residual pending human policy choice and interagency coordination.
levers.residual_reason: The stated minimum lever ('cross-reference manual to the rule; avoid restating') is a single RESOLVE_CROSS_REFERENCE, but the v2.1 lever text expands the scope to 'resolve the two unreconciled pending rewrites ... before they compound the layering' — a reconciliation of two conflicting pending rulemakings (a 2024 freestanding board-oversight standard + annual ratification vs a 2026 approval-by-board/equivalent-body/senior-management rule). That reconciliation is not one primitive and does not match any of the four named composites: it requires resolving a substantive policy conflict between competing proposed standards (which body approves; whether an annual ratification duty exists) that the source does not settle. Neither the direction of the substitution/assignment nor which duty survives is fixed by the provided text, so no determinate primitive composition can be anchored.

levers.min_reform_lever: Coordinate CMS expectations; CFPB now lightly enforced (2026).
levers.rationale: The minimum reform lever text 'Coordinate CMS expectations' is a pure-coordination action, not a structural consolidation. The source itself frames the distinct mandates as legally distinct ('CFPB consumer mandate vs. prudential safety-and-soundness'), and no roadmap row supplies an actor, instrument, or authority to support any binding structural primitive. No verbatim text supports MERGE, CANONICALIZE_DEFINITION, DEEM_SATISFIED, or any other primitive; the lever is a coordinate/clarify action, so is_consolidation is false and no operations are returned. normative_kinds noted for human review because coordinating across CFPB and prudential regulators is interagency coordination bearing a supervisory value judgment about how much weight consumer-compliance oversight receives.

levers.min_reform_lever: One interagency real-estate-lending standard; fold ACL/credit-review into the risk-committee credit cycle.
levers.rationale: The lever merges the duplicative Real Estate Lending Standards (parts 208/365/34), the ACL policy statement, and credit-risk-review guidance into one interagency standard folded into the risk-committee credit cycle — a MERGE + CANONICALIZE_DEFINITION + RESOLVE_CROSS_REFERENCE consolidation. The Real Estate Lending Standards live in parallel agency appendices (208/365/34), so the pathway is joint FRB/OCC/FDIC rulemaking. Insider-credit (Reg O) and affiliate (Reg W) approvals are 'legally distinct' — they 'protect the insured bank specifically' — and are excluded from the merge; their underlying statutes (371c/375b) are proposed as floor candidates for a human to own.

levers.min_reform_lever: Consolidate into Reg YY; OCC incorporates by reference.
levers.rationale: Per the source: 'Consolidate into Reg YY; OCC incorporates by reference' and 'Board approval of the same individual's appointment/pay at two levels' is duplicative, but 'Bank-level independence-of-CRE-from-front-line structure is an OCC-specific control' is legally distinct and must be retained. The retained distinct OCC control alongside the consolidation of the duplicative board approval does not close under a single primitive or one of the four composites. Overlapping sources 'Reg YY 252.33(b); OCC App. D I.E.7' name both FRB and OCC as actors; a binding cross-agency consolidation with OCC incorporation-by-reference requires joint rulemaking. No roadmap row was provided, so the lawful pathway and statutory obstacles are not settled by the source; instrument marked as the coordinated pathway the two named regimes imply, but no statutory floor candidate is asserted absent supporting text.
levers.residual_reason: The lever bundles two structurally distinct actions that no single primitive or named composite captures: (1) consolidating the duplicative board-approval of the same individual's appointment/pay into Reg YY with OCC incorporation-by-reference (a MERGE + RESOLVE_CROSS_REFERENCE or DEEM_SATISFIED shape), while (2) preserving the legally distinct OCC-specific independence-of-CRE-from-front-line control as a retained non-target. The consolidation-plus-retained-distinct-control combination does not match any of the four composites (consolidation, master_direction_build, board_role_clarification, vertical_rationalization), and the source text does not settle which primitive expresses the OCC incorporation-by-reference (whether the two duties both survive for DEEM_SATISFIED or whether one is repealed via MERGE). Marking residual rather than guessing.

levers.min_reform_lever: Single interagency change-in-director notice procedure.

operands: change in director / senior executive officer

levers.rationale: The lever is a 'single interagency change-in-director notice procedure' folding parallel FRB/OCC 914 notice regimes. This maps to the consolidation composite (MERGE + CANONICALIZE_DEFINITION + RESOLVE_CROSS_REFERENCE). The statutory disqualification (12 U.S.C. 1829, FDIA 8) and Call Report attestation are noted as legally distinct, low-burden duties that survive and are not consolidation targets; only the parallel notice regimes are merged. Because the notice duties themselves derive from statute (12 U.S.C. 1831i), a binding merged procedure requires joint rulemaking by FRB and OCC.

levers.min_reform_lever: Single cross-referenced prudential independence definition.
levers.rationale: The minimum reform lever is stated as a 'Single cross-referenced prudential independence definition,' which maps to CANONICALIZE_DEFINITION (a single/uniform definition across regimes). The text flags 'Different lookback periods and affiliation tests reflect different statutory lineages' and lists overlapping sources including OCC App. D III.D, Reg YY 252.33(a)(4), FDICIA, SOX 301, DFA 952, and exchange listing — implicating multiple agencies (FRB + OCC + FDIC + SEC) and cross-regulator coordination via 'Joint interagency statement + SEC coordination.' Because the source describes coordination through an interagency statement rather than binding rulemaking, instrument_required is interagency_statement; differing statutory lineages drive the statutory_constraint and interagency_coordination normative kinds.

The structural need — merge overlapping general director-training obligations while factoring out the legally distinct topic-specific BSA training — exceeds a single primitive and does not match the primitive set of any of the four named composites, so the honest finding is residual.

levers.min_reform_lever: Permit the §36/Part 363 audit committee to satisfy the fiduciary-audit duty where composition overlaps.
levers.rationale: The minimum reform lever is 'Permit the §36/Part 363 audit committee to satisfy the fiduciary-audit duty where composition overlaps.' This is a deem-satisfied by cross-reference: the fiduciary-audit committee duty (12 CFR part 9) survives but is treated as satisfied where the §36/Part 363 audit committee (which also survives) overlaps in composition. The condition 'where composition overlaps' is quoted from the source. Part 9 is an OCC rule; the pathway is APA rulemaking. No roadmap row was provided, so actor/instrument are inferred from the overlapping OCC source and left minimal; the source does not name an agency, but 12 CFR part 9 is OCC's fiduciary rule.

levers.min_reform_lever: Finalize one 956 framework or rely on guidance; SEC independence satisfies the prudential element.
levers.rationale: Source states DFA 956 is 'unimplemented' / an 'unfinished rule' and the reform requires a six-agency final rule or statutory repeal, with FRB/SEC having 'previously declined.' Because the target text is a not-yet-enacted mandate and the lever is a policy choice among finalize/guidance/repeal paths, it exceeds the fixed 16-primitive/4-composite closure and is an honest residual. SEC comp-committee independence is noted as legally distinct (serves investors), reinforcing that the overlap is not a clean consolidation target.
levers.residual_reason: The lever offers a disjunctive choice ('finalize one 956 framework OR rely on guidance') requiring a six-agency policy decision to complete an unimplemented statutory mandate, not a mechanical structural consolidation of existing enacted text. Completing an unfinished DFA §956 rulemaking (or electing to abandon it in favor of guidance) is a discretionary interagency policy act that no primitive expresses; the calculus operates on enacted overlapping duties, and §956 duties are 'unimplemented.' The additional claim that 'SEC independence satisfies the prudential element' would suggest DEEM_SATISFIED, but the SEC comp-committee independence duty and the prudential §956 duty serve distinct purposes (investor protection vs. safety-and-soundness) and one duty (the §956 rule) does not yet exist to be deemed-satisfying, so no both-survive deem relation can be anchored.

levers.min_reform_lever: One enterprise info-security program approval; joint SEC/banking statement on cyber oversight. v2.1: the 36-hour interagency incident-notification rule and the SEC cyber-disclosure regime impose non-aligned timelines on the same incident — harmonization here is selection of a single operational standard, not deletion.

operands: 12 CFR 30 App. B + three parallel appendices

levers.rationale: The consolidation portion matches the consolidation composite by primitive set, but the source explicitly adds a distinct cross-regime harmonization component (SEC cyber-disclosure vs. 36-hour interagency notification) that is "selection of a single operational standard, not deletion" and that the text keeps legally distinct in purpose. Because the lever cannot be reduced to a single primitive or exactly one of the four composites, it is a residual.
levers.residual_reason: The lever bundles two structurally distinct actions that no single named composite covers: (1) a consolidation of the four parallel GLBA 501(b) appendices (MERGE + CANONICALIZE_DEFINITION + RESOLVE_CROSS_REFERENCE), AND (2) harmonization of two non-aligned incident-notification/disclosure timelines described as "selection of a single operational standard, not deletion" spanning the banking 36-hour rule and the SEC cyber-disclosure regime. The second action crosses the prudential/investor-protection boundary (the SEC disclosure "serves investors; the prudential program serves safety-and-soundness"), and the timeline-selection is not a MERGE, CANONICALIZE_DEFINITION, or ASSIGN_DUTY_PARAMETER of a single retained duty — it is a cross-agency reconciliation of two surviving, legally distinct obligations. No single primitive or one of the four composites expresses the combined consolidation-plus-cross-regime-timeline-selection lever.

levers.min_reform_lever: Single 'resilience planning' board cycle; shared resolution submission with an IDI annex.
levers.rationale: Source describes 'Multiple board-approved resilience plans on different cycles' and 'parent and IDI resolution submissions overlap heavily' as duplicative, while 'The FDIC's interest in resolving the insured bank even if the parent's plan fails is genuinely distinct (parallel-but-justified).' The reform 'Single resilience planning board cycle; shared resolution submission with an IDI annex' therefore mixes cadence alignment, partial merge, and a retained parallel-distinct obligation across two statutes (DFA 165(d)/Reg QQ, FDI Act/360.10) plus Reg YY 252.34(b) and SR 14-8. Because a distinct FDIC interest is explicitly preserved, the merge is incomplete, and no single primitive or named composite matches the composite of cadence + partial-merge + preserved-parallel. Marked residual honestly.
levers.residual_reason: The lever bundles two structurally different moves that no single primitive or named composite captures: (1) collapsing multiple board-approved resilience/recovery plans onto one cycle (a cadence/parameter move plus MERGE of overlapping approvals), and (2) creating a shared resolution submission where the FDIC IDI interest is retained as a genuinely distinct annex ('parallel-but-justified'). The FDIC's distinct interest in resolving the insured bank even if the parent's plan fails means this is NOT a clean MERGE (the IDI submission survives as a distinct annex), nor is it vertical_rationalization (no entity_level_mirror + DEEM_SATISFIED + FACTOR_EXCEPTION pattern fits the 'shared submission with retained-distinct annex' shape). It combines a cadence-alignment across cycles, a partial merge of overlapping content, and a preserved parallel-distinct obligation \u2014 a mixture that spans authorities under two separate statutes and cannot be reduced to one primitive or one of the four composites.
